In July 2024 I decided to take a course. I bought it with mentorship support and deeply regretted it. The course was recorded back in 2022 and is packed with outdated information that has nothing to do with today's reality. From the very first modules you'll run into trouble setting up a store. You'll be watching a lesson and won't be able to follow along because the Shopify interface is completely different now. You'll waste your time not deepening your knowledge but hunting for buttons that no longer exist. Support from Artur is barely useful; the curator has zero interest in your results, and neither does the school itself. In every single module there are additional costs for a pile of other apps without which you simply can't move forward. I find it deeply dishonest not to disclose this on the webinars where the organizers sell this course. The subscriptions add up to quite a significant sum. Then comes product selection and advertising — with their own surprises and secrets. First you have to pick a product, analyze it — which takes a lot of time — and you need at least 5 such products, and then essentially launch ads on them blind (because only the test will show whether you guessed right), with no guarantees, running a three-day test at up to $150 per product, and then hope for the best…

Everyone has to decide for themselves, but here's my summary:

1. The course is full of outdated information — it might technically work, but studying it is maximally difficult and infuriating.

2. You have to buy a ton of different apps, subscriptions, and other things. Significant additional costs that nobody warns you about — they'll be a surprise in every module.

3. Mentorship support is worthless — very weak and very short (just one month; they may extend it because there was a backlash about this). No replies on weekends or after 6 or 7 PM. During power outages it was extremely difficult, and they take no responsibility for that. Understandable, but the students aren't to blame either — they're hostages of the situation.

4. Product selection and launch is a lottery.

If you have a pile of time and money — in the literal sense, a PILE of these resources — you can give it a shot. If not, think a hundred times.

Very disappointed with this experience. Worst training I've ever done — but what's done is done.

Be careful and read the reviews before you buy! Peace to everyone!
